summary: Among equity rows with n>=4, Europe (8.1%, n=4) and EM (8.0%, n=7) lead; global 6.8% (n=6), US small cap 6.5% (n=6), Japan 6.4% (n=4); US large cap trails at 6.0% (n=8).
Fixed income holds the tightest IQRs among rows with n>=4: EM local debt 5.3% (IQR 20bp), IG corporate 5.4% (23bp), intermediate Treasuries 4.9% (24bp), high yield 5.9% (27bp); cash 3.7% (n=6).
Ranked by IQR (rows with n>=4), the widest disagreements are EM equity (250bp), commodities (171bp), US small cap (165bp) and private equity (155bp), which also has the top median, 9.7%.
US large cap spans 1.7-7.6% around a 6.0% median (n=8); the split is valuation drag (Ninety One, Invesco, Vanguard, below) versus AI-boosted earnings (BNY Investments, Fidelity International, above).

High yield's numbers are tight (IQR 27bp, n=8) but stances split: PIMCO and Amundi underweight, Goldman Sachs AM and UBS GWM CIO overweight; in private credit, PIMCO's high-conviction underweight faces a mostly overweight field.
This site's LTCMA trails public medians most on commodities (3.5% vs 5.7%, n=7), UK equity (7.0% vs 8.9%, n=3), China equity (7.4% vs 8.5%, n=3) and US high yield (5.0% vs 5.9%, n=8).

Prediction markets side with higher-for-longer calls (Invesco, BlackRock Investment Institute): a 25bp hike at the next FOMC is priced at 91.5% on both venues, zero 2026 cuts at 98.4% (Polymarket) to 99.0% (Kalshi).

That pricing contradicts Goldman Sachs AM's soft-landing case of possibly two 2026 cuts and Mercer's accommodative-policy view; 2026 US recession is priced at 1.5% (Kalshi) and 2.4% (Polymarket), consistent with resilient-growth calls.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap: valuation drag versus AI earnings, 1.7-7.6% around a 6.0% median (n=8)

bull.argument: Above the 6.0% median, up to BNY Investments' 7.6%: BNY assumes AI-lifted earnings-share growth with flat multiples; Fidelity International cites AI-driven revenue, dividends and buybacks. Goldman Sachs AM and BlackRock Investment Institute are overweight on mega-cap earnings and AI productivity, though the Institute's November table cut US equities to neutral. AQR and T. Rowe Price land above despite rich valuations.
bull.data_used: Earnings and revenue growth boosted by AI, dividend and buyback yield, real GDP and inflation; BNY Investments holds valuation multiples constant rather than assuming mean reversion.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to Ninety One's 1.7%, a record low on negative revaluation. Invesco's valuation drag stays material despite tech earnings and buybacks; for Vanguard, high valuations damp stronger earnings; State Street's building blocks include multiple change. PIMCO sees a negligible equity risk premium versus bonds, Lazard doubts US resilience and expects rotation away, and Amundi is underweight.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations and assumed multiple contraction, revaluation impact on long-run returns, and the equity risk premium relative to bond yields.

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether AI-driven earnings growth validates current multiples: forward EPS revisions, profit margins versus long-run equilibrium, and the earnings yield gap to Treasuries.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap: 165bp IQR, split over whether small caps beat large caps; median 6.5% (n=6)

bull.argument: Above the 6.5% median, up to BNY Investments' 7.5%. Vanguard (after third-quarter weakness) and AQR rank small caps above their own large-cap figures; BNY lands high despite a weak size premium, since its broad US equity view is high. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on valuations, expected rate cuts, accelerating earnings and renewed M&A.
bull.data_used: Valuations, earnings acceleration, expected rate cuts and M&A (Goldman Sachs AM); AQR's real return plus inflation; BNY Investments' factor model with a weak size premium.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to State Street's 5.0%. State Street, Invesco and T. Rowe Price each put small caps under their own large-cap figures. Invesco cites weaker long-run earnings growth despite a smaller valuation drag; T. Rowe Price upgraded the segment from its prior edition but stays valuation-anchored. No publisher is underweight.
bear.data_used: Building blocks of dividend yield, real earnings growth and multiple change; lower long-term small-cap earnings growth; valuation-anchored forecasts.

divergences.what_to_watch: Small-cap earnings growth relative to large caps and refinancing costs; Goldman Sachs AM's rate-cut premise faces zero 2026 cuts priced at 99.0% (Kalshi) and 98.4% (Polymarket).

divergences.label: EM equity
divergences.headline: EM equity: earnings and weaker-dollar optimism versus revaluation risk; widest IQR (250bp) among rows with n>=4

bull.argument: Above the 8.0% median, up to Robeco's 8.8%; both top figures (Robeco, T. Rowe Price) are five-year horizons. BNY Investments cites the largest real-GDP lift to earnings plus dollar weakness. Goldman Sachs AM adds Fed cuts and a wide P/E discount to the US; BlackRock Investment Institute cites earnings, cheaper valuations and AI supply-chain exposure. Amundi and CIBC are overweight.
bull.data_used: Forward earnings momentum, real GDP contribution to earnings, a weaker dollar, Fed easing assumptions and the P/E discount to US equities.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to Ninety One's 3.7%, a hedged figure in the bottom quartile of its history on negative revaluation. Vanguard raised its view on easing valuations and better fundamentals yet stays below the median, flagging the highest volatility among equities. Invesco is unchanged, with currency and dividend support but outcomes tied to earnings delivery and country valuations.
bear.data_used: Revaluation from current multiples, currency-hedged returns versus history, volatility, and dependence on earnings delivery and country-level valuations.

divergences.what_to_watch: EM earnings revisions, the dollar and the P/E discount to the US; Goldman Sachs AM's assumed Fed cuts are priced out: zero 2026 cuts at 99.0% (Kalshi), 98.4% (Polymarket).

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: tight numbers (IQR 27bp, n=8) but stances split on defaults versus income

bull.argument: Above the 5.9% median, up to Ninety One's 6.3%, lifted by higher Treasury yields rather than spreads; BNY Investments nets defaults off yield while assuming spreads widen toward their long-run median. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight given solid interest cover, contained defaults, an improved ratings mix and M&A support; UBS GWM CIO, region unspecified, values high yield's income.
bull.data_used: Higher starting Treasury yields, yield net of expected default losses, interest coverage, default trends and ratings mix; BNY Investments already assumes spread widening.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to AQR's 5.0%, built as real return plus expected inflation. T. Rowe Price expects spread widening to eat part of the carry; State Street haircuts yields and spreads for default probability. PIMCO, underweight, reads tight spreads as complacency as defaults rise and AI threatens leveraged legacy borrowers, in a late credit cycle. Amundi is underweight.
bear.data_used: Tight spreads versus a rising default trend, default-adjusted yield models, and AQR's real-return-plus-inflation build.

divergences.what_to_watch: Realized US high-yield default and loss rates versus spread levels: rising defaults with spreads still tight would support PIMCO; contained defaults would support Goldman Sachs AM.

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities: 171bp IQR around a 5.7% median (n=7); futures-premium models versus low, thinly explained forecasts

bull.argument: Above the 5.7% median, up to AQR's 6.7%, built from a futures excess return over cash plus the real cash return. Invesco cites inflation and supply-shock sensitivity; Robeco ties outcomes to conflicts and the dollar. UBS GWM CIO is overweight as a hedge against supply and inflation risk, with structural demand from power grids, data centers and electrification.
bull.data_used: Long-run futures excess return over cash plus real cash yield (AQR), inflation and supply-shock sensitivity, and structural demand from electrification and data centers.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to BNY Investments' 2.3%, a low, high-volatility figure little changed on the year whose drivers BNY does not explain; T. Rowe Price also gives no rationale. Only State Street details a build: US inflation and dollar forecasts, futures roll return, positioning and collateral return. No publisher is underweight.
bear.data_used: State Street's inputs: US inflation and dollar-index forecasts, futures roll return, positioning and collateral return; BNY Investments and T. Rowe Price disclose no drivers.

divergences.what_to_watch: Futures roll yield and realized inflation versus T-bill collateral returns; the 25bp hike priced at 91.5% on both venues would lift the collateral component.

divergences.label: Global govt bonds
divergences.headline: Global government bonds: narrow numbers (IQR 39bp, n=4) but stances split on fiscal strain versus diversification

bull.argument: Above the 5.1% median, both at the 5.3% range top on USD-hedged composites: Robeco says higher yields lifted expected returns, though not without risk; Ninety One puts developed sovereign returns near the centre of their history. PIMCO's highest-conviction overweight rests on desynchronized cycles and diverging policy, creating diversification and country and curve opportunities from attractive starting yields.
bull.data_used: Starting yields hedged to USD, cross-country cycle and policy divergence, and curve and country-selection opportunities.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to Fidelity International's 4.8%, which sits low despite Fidelity's overweight: it sees income as the main driver and sovereigns diversifying in recessionary shocks. Invesco's figure rests on income from starting yields. BNY Investments, underweight, argues fiscal strain weakens sovereigns' risk-adjusted appeal and points to real assets and private markets for diversification.
bear.data_used: Income from current yield curves, fiscal strain on sovereign balance sheets, and the relative appeal of real assets and private markets as diversifiers.

divergences.what_to_watch: Stock-bond correlation during equity drawdowns, term premia under fiscal strain, and cross-country policy divergence, with the Fed's next move priced as a 25bp hike at 91.5% on both venues.

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity: illiquidity premium versus levered public equity net of fees; 6.6-10.5% around a 9.7% median (n=5)

bull.argument: Above the 9.7% median, up to BNY Investments' 10.5%: BNY adds a strong illiquidity premium to public-equity factor exposure, with private capital funding AI innovation and infrastructure. T. Rowe Price, on a five-year horizon, credits the illiquidity premium and active management. UBS GWM CIO is overweight operationally focused private equity and secondaries; CIBC Asset Management is also overweight.
bull.data_used: Public-equity factor exposure plus an illiquidity premium, Cambridge Associates Global PE history, active management, and private capital's role financing AI and infrastructure.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to AQR's 6.6%, a levered dividend-discount model of US buyouts net of heavy fees; cheaper debt and multiple expansion lifted it, yet AQR still sees compressed premia in private assets. State Street extrapolates historical fund returns, which after fees roughly match leverage-adjusted listed equity, implying little premium beyond leverage. No publisher is underweight.
bear.data_used: Levered dividend-discount model with fee drag and financing costs (AQR); extrapolated fund history benchmarked to leverage-adjusted listed equity (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Net-of-fee buyout returns against leverage-adjusted public equity, exit and distribution activity, and buyout debt costs, whose decline lifted AQR's estimate.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit: PIMCO's high-conviction underweight versus a mostly overweight field; 5.0-9.2% around a 7.0% median (n=4)

bull.argument: Above the 7.0% median: T. Rowe Price's five-year 9.2% (range top) rests on an illiquidity premium and structural demand for private capital; State Street's net-of-fee senior-debt figure is unexplained. Goldman Sachs AM cites a yield pickup over public credit and a lower default history than syndicated loans. BlackRock Investment Institute, Amundi and CIBC Asset Management are overweight, the Institute selectively.
bull.data_used: Illiquidity premium and Cliffwater Direct Lending history (T. Rowe Price), yield spread over public credit, and historical default rates versus syndicated loans.

bear.argument: Below the median, down to AQR's 5.0%: modeled as levered floating-rate high yield, fees absorb any illiquidity premium, and tighter spreads and lower cash rates cut it. Fidelity International is overweight but sits just below the median, seeing no immediate stress. PIMCO's high-conviction underweight cites maturity extensions, PIK use and financial engineering in direct lending, expecting much higher losses.
bear.data_used: Stress signals in direct lending (maturity extensions, PIK, financial engineering) and AQR's levered floating-rate high-yield proxy net of fees, sensitive to spreads and cash rates.

divergences.what_to_watch: Direct-lending non-accruals, PIK share and realized losses; the 25bp hike priced at 91.5% on both venues would lift floating-rate income and borrower strain alike.
